道德爭議爆發：重現「No Russian」的殘酷考驗

真正將輿論推向高潮的是關卡中的屠村搜查劇情，讓許多玩家聯想到當年的震撼任務「No Russian」。作者描述玩家在任務中扮演北韓無名士兵，被迫搜捕並處決村民以證明忠誠。遊戲設計了極為沉重的沉浸機制，若玩家抗命拒絕處決、私自放走藏匿的平民，或是射擊牆上的最高領導人畫像，都會被同袍當場處決。這種描寫軍令難違的極端壓迫感，引發了大量實況主與玩家的情緒反彈與倫理爭議。

針對部分實況主因抗拒虛擬處決而引發的不滿，知名實況主xQc與眾多老玩家嘲諷這代玩家過於脆弱且雙標，質疑大眾在多人模式殺敵無數，卻在單人戰役對一場虛構處決產生道德危機。此外，為了應對敏感爭議，部分如日本版等發行版本則選擇直接刪除或跳過處決鏡頭。最後，儘管動視高層公開將本作與《GTA 6》並列為年度最強遊戲的言論遭到社群譏笑，但該作在Steam創下自2010年《黑色行動》以來的高評價，並帶動系列突破11萬在線人數，展現出驚人的討論熱度與成功。

The Call of Duty series is often mocked as a yearly product; its declining quality year. after year and formulaic design have left players weary of the franchise, with last year’s Black Ops seeing poor results. Yet, players never expected that just one year later, the newest Call of Duty entry, Modern Warfare IV, would completely shock everyone. Even before its official launch, the campaign mode sparked massive community discussion, even racking up over 2,000 "Very Positive" reviews on Steam. Activision executives even publicly declared it the game of the year, claiming it’s not Nintendo’s Zelda, but theirs and GTA. 6. Who invited that kid? >> So, what exactly happened? Why did Call of Duty: Modern Warfare IV trigger such intense discussion in the player community? Today, Player Confidential is here to share the controversy surrounding Activision’s annual " Modern Warfare" release. If there’s anything I missed or anything you’d like to add, feel free to leave a comment below. Before we start the video, make sure to like and subscribe to our channel, and don't forget to ring the bell so you don't miss our updates. Let's get started! Call of Duty: Modern Warfare IV serves as the 23rd entry in the COD series and the. fourth installment in the rebooted Modern Warfare sub-series. The campaign theme this time takes us to Korea, allowing players to experience a conflict between North and South Korea. As always, this installment leans on its campaign as a selling point while focusing on multiplayer for long-term operations. And the price tag is still something a poor player like me can't afford; instead of playing this FPS, I’d rather buy the whole collection of cat-girl FPS games. Although the game hasn't officially launched, pre-order players got early access to the full campaign starting October 16th.

. This campaign immediately ignited widespread discussion and received very positive reviews, with many players stating that the "classic COD feel" is back. It’s all out now. As the saying goes, the higher the expectations, the greater the disappointment. But when disappointment is already the norm, expectations are low, leading people to jump in with no expectations and find it surprisingly good. All things considered, that was one of the better Call of Duty campaigns. I think the middle of it was kind of a slog, but. the intro was super hype compared to most modern Call of Duty and the ending was pretty solid. I never really expect much but that was good overall. >> This campaign is set primarily on the Korean Peninsula, depicting a fictional conflict involving a full-scale invasion of South Korea by North Korea. The game's visual performance feels ultra-realistic to players, and the actors 'facial motion capture is also impeccable. Whether it's the performance of Barry Sloane or Lanny Joon as Farah, both have greatly enhanced the game's intense sense of immersion. The news is that Zebra is back, but the good news is that this time, he's only responsible for the. voice acting. The level of detail in the convenience store scene is so high that players can't help but wander around slowly, and with the boost from DLSS 3, some players almost can't distinguish between the game and reality. We are no longer just playing games in this era; we are playing through movies. This is the most realistic supermarket I have ever seen in a game. But what truly made Modern Warfare the center of attention is the village massacre plot in the campaign, which reminded many players of the classic "No Russian" mission that shocked the community back then. >> In this mission, to find a traitor,. players take on the role of a nameless soldier and must demonstrate loyalty by following orders to round up and interrogate all the villagers. Whether they knew something or not, they were killed, leaving players shocked by such cruel and extreme actions, while also questioning if the development team is smearing North Korea—even North Korean players didn't complain. That goes to show the game is well-made; the General wouldn't secretly buy a copy to play at home, would he? Is the only account in North Korea actually playing it? We really need an actual review from the only North Korean player. Of course, the game also hides many.

details and easter eggs. As a North Korean soldier, if you choose to shoot at the portrait of the Supreme Leader on the wall, your teammates will immediately take you down, the reason being that you brought shame to the country. When the mission requires players to execute villagers, the system actually provides an option to refuse, but the price is being deemed disloyal and getting executed by your comrades. The cutscene shows the soldier you control falling in the background; this design presents the helplessness of North Korean soldiers who must obey orders. The entire mission makes immersed players feel. extremely uncomfortable, and if you spare a girl hiding in the cellar, you will later be held responsible for not clearing the house thoroughly, ultimately paying a painful price. The outstanding performance has led players to call it the best "Call of Duty" campaign in a long time, and even players like me who can't afford the game couldn't wait to watch a playthrough. Even more bizarre is that rumors of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un's passing recently surfaced, forcing state media to rush and release photos to prove he is still alive. Meanwhile, tensions on the border. between North and South Korea continue to escalate, with Kim Yo-jong warning that if the South Korean military continues its provocations, further action will not be ruled out. This coincidence led players to jokingly suggest, "It seems the General pre-ordered Modern Warfare III and finished the campaign first. Is the only Steam user in North Korea really done with the story?" But as discussions about the campaign mode grew, controversies followed. Beyond some players feeling the plot was too aggressive and full of plot holes. regarding North Korea, international players were up in arms over the village massacre scene. Many streamers expressed dissatisfaction with having to participate in these actions, feeling the game forced them to do it. Stop. >> Meanwhile, some players said they couldn't bring themselves to do it, emphasizing that even knowing the choices in the game are fictional, they didn't want to make decisions that went against their conscience to complete the objective. One streamer was even in.

the middle of a live broadcast when a fan sent a gift that sent them straight on a "hell train." Don't laugh, don't laugh, don't laugh. Many players found the reactions of these streamers somewhat funny; after all, the "No Russian" mission back in the day was even more extreme. How can you not handle killing one person in this campaign mode? Streamer xQc even retorted directly, questioning how people have no problem racking up points in multiplayer but suddenly have a moral crisis when they have to shoot one person in the campaign. Let me log. in and just kill 60,000 people. because violence is dis point in the game over years but you have to hang one guy >> Seeing players complain, others mocked them, saying, "Don't let Logan Paul see this," and calling this generation of gamers too "fragile." This is Call of Duty—haven't they always done things like this before? I am really sick of. these fake outraged reactions. Why does everyone want to play bad games? Back in 2009, nobody cared about these things because it was just a game. Hey, hey, stop, stop, stop me first. So, is this the most "normal" type of COD player? However, Modern Warfare III is actually similar to "No Russian" back in the day, with some regions censoring or modifying sensitive content. In the original "No Russian" mission, if players were using the Japanese or German versions, they were prohibited from shooting civilians; firing a. single shot resulted in mission failure . This time, the Japanese version also forbids shooting, and the execution scene is skipped entirely. Not long ago , a senior Activision marketing executive mentioned in an interview that they didn't mean to offend The Legend of Zelda, but the two biggest and hottest games of 2026 are actually GTA 6 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. He gave the reason that GTA 6 would get more people to turn on their consoles, dusting off their Xbox and PlayStation units to start gaming again , which would undoubtedly bring them more traffic. Wait, hold on—is he.

throwing shade at consoles for gathering dust because they have no games to play? As soon as he said this, the gaming community immediately reacted. Everyone felt like Modern Warfare was an uninvited clown, wondering how it could even include itself in the discussion for the best games, and they were speechless. If we're comparing file size, then he's actually right. This just goes to show they don't understand the gaming community at all. A game that truly deserves the title of "Greatest Game of All Time" versus a pile of cold vomit —it perfectly recreated the Jujutsu Kaisen script. Everyone was discussing. who would win between the strongest in history and the strongest of today, only for Activision execs to suddenly jump in, while the internal thought of the Modern COD studio is just, "I’m in danger." But to be fair, the success of Modern Warfare III was truly unexpected for players. It is currently the highest-rated Call of Duty title on the Steam platform since Call of Duty: Black Ops in 2010. At the same time, the release of the campaign mode helped the Call of Duty series peak player count break through 110,000, a peak that even surpassed the launch numbers. of Black Ops 6 on the Steam platform. Looking back at the state of Call of Duty over the past few years, ever since the series entered the era of highly commercialized annual releases, its reputation has been going downhill, arguably getting worse every year. Of course, Activision itself admitted that Call of Duty: Black Ops 6—wait, that the previous entry failed to meet the studio's expectations; its subpar single-player campaign made it the lowest-rated entry in the series on Metacritic over the years. The main goal of deciding to make this Modern Warfare was to return the series to a more solid military shooter experience, while maintaining both cinematic feel. and realism. However, players remained skeptical about this "return to military shooters," as the Call of Duty battlefield has been filled with crossover skins for years now. Seeing Snoop Dogg, Godzilla, or Gundam running around with guns is no longer surprising, and these excessive crossovers have truly annoyed many veteran players, negatively impacting both sales and the community's perception. So when the trailer for Modern Warfare was first released, the comments section was filled with cynical mockery from the gaming community. I think the funniest part is that they made the game's trailer super.

serious, but the moment the game launched, there were goofy, bizarre skin packs available on day one. I can't wait to fight John Wick while wearing a Baby Shark skin, and I'm itching to play Peter Griffin in Season 2. Peter, what are you doing? Crack! >> After seeing the lackluster sales and criticism over the past few years, Activision realized they need to win back core players, so they decided to add a skin-toggling feature to let players hide these crossover outfits. In simple terms, it's like a transmog concept; if you don't like crossover. skins, just hide them. As a player who specifically buys obnoxious skins in FPS games just to annoy my opponents, I absolutely don't support this feature. What if, in the future, I only... Brother >> Actually, players dislike crossover skins because they ruin the sense of immersion in a war game. By introducing this feature, the developers are purely addressing the immediate problem, but they still haven't solved the players' dissatisfaction with the excessive number of crossover collaborations. You , if you let people turn off all of your skins because of how bad they are,. isn't that kind of like an indication that you went in the wrong direction? >> But if the collaboration was for a top-tier goddess skin, as a gentleman, I would definitely not hide it. If the developers could also offer an option to hide skirts and trigger a "damaged clothing" state, then wow! Modern Warfare III’s campaign mode has pleasantly surprised many players, and even the Zombie mode and DMZ experience have unexpectedly received decent feedback, though bug issues remain abundant. Oh my god! Oh my god! Oh my. god! Oh my god! >> Of course, one of the most classic traditions in COD multiplayer is the trash-talking session between players. This not only doubles the gaming experience but can even end racism. If you don't believe me, just watch what happens when an Indian player and a Black player start trash-talking each other. Don't you don't run something? Don't you pay support? >> Don't you know how to clean your feet? Don't you left over the KFC chicken.

Don't you have some clothes to put on. Don't you got some watermelon? Honestly , I think the Indian going to come out ahead, bro. Honestly, I think this is running out. I think he's going out already. Don't you have a monkey? Yes, it is. By the way, this is how you racism. >> For a Call of Duty series that has become highly commercialized and seen its reputation decline in recent years,. Modern Warfare III has certainly brought some relatively positive changes. Interestingly, the Halo community was worried just a while ago that the Halo IP would be handed over to COD-related teams for development, but now that Modern Warfare III has unexpectedly received good feedback, it might allow some Halo fans to put down their guard and look forward to the future of the series a bit more. However, it is too early to jump to conclusions; remaining skeptical is exactly what players should be doing. The current positive feedback can only be considered a decent start; it’s not enough to prove it is a successful title. This feedback might just prove. that what players have always truly loved about COD is its campaign mode. As for confirming whether Modern Warfare III is a successful work, the real key still lies in whether the multiplayer mode and DMZ can maintain their quality after the official launch , and what kind of performance they will deliver through long-term operations. Will it start strong only to fizzle out, or will its reputation continue to climb? What are your thoughts on this modern-style warfare? Do you feel that this entry is truly better than those of the past? Feel free to share in the comments below, and join our Patreon for some amazing. adult-oriented games.

applicability of these terms in specific jurisdictions remain contingent on the circumstances, as regulations on reverse engineering vary by region; some areas permit it for interoperability or compatibility, while others impose stricter limitations. Most of the ported games, backward-compatible classics, and decompiled projects players see online currently adopt a strategy of requiring players to provide their own. legitimate copies, which is effectively a way to minimize legal risk. Nowadays, players can not only find Naughty Dog’s classic Jak and Daxter but also play 25-year-old games like E.C. on PC platforms. These projects not only manage to preserve the core content of the original games but also add modern features like high-resolution support and widescreen, allowing players to run games directly on PC without relying on traditional emulators; some even support devices like the Steam Deck. PC project as an example, players must prepare the PS2 European PAL version game disc image and import the file upon first launch to extract the data needed to run the game. Leaderboards that were once used to motivate developers to track project progress have now devolved into a competition concerned only with numbers and completion speed.
